35: client; they never start one. Before running a script, start the headless lite
36: client in the background and leave it running:
37:

40: ```

43: process per bot; it exits non-zero if the game session ends. Without it, a
44: script exits with `No game client is attached`. MCP `execute_code` doesn't need

# RS-Agent Bot Guide

You're here to play the mmo game through the progressive development of botting scripts, starting small then adapting to your desires and ideas.
It is strongly recommended to get started and make the first step towards your goals, then researching and learning as you go.

## First Time Setup

**Create a new bot using the setup script:**

Ask the user for a bot name (max 12 chars, alphanumeric). If they skip, use the command without a username to auto-generate a random 9-character name.

```bash
# With custom username
bun bots/create-bot.ts {username}

# Auto-generate random username
bun bots/create-bot.ts

# Use local server (sets SERVER=localhost in bot.env)
bun bots/create-bot.ts {username} --local

# Use a custom server
bun bots/create-bot.ts {username} --server=myserver.example.com
```

This automatically creates:

- `bots/{username}/bot.env` - Credentials with auto-generated password
- `bots/{username}/lab_log.md` - Session notes template
- `bots/{username}/script.ts` - Ready-to-run starter script

### Start a Game Client (scripts only)

Scripts (`bun bots/{username}/*.ts`) and `bun sdk/cli.ts` need a running game
client; they never start one. Before running a script, start the headless lite
client in the background and leave it running:

```bash
cd server/webclient && bun install && bun src/lite/runner.ts {username}
```

It logs `Gateway connected, registering as '{username}'` once it's ready. One
process per bot; it exits non-zero if the game session ends. Without it, a
script exits with `No game client is attached`. MCP `execute_code` doesn't need
this step; it opens a browser client itself.

### Quick Start

1. Install dependencies: `bun install` (from project root)
2. Open project in your AI coding tool — the MCP server will be available automatically
3. Control your bot with suggestions.

### Tools

| Tool                           | Description                                    |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `execute_code(bot_name, code)` | Run code on a bot. Auto-connects on first use. |
| `list_bots()`                  | List connected bots                            |
| `disconnect_bot(name)`         | Disconnect a bot                               |

### Example

```typescript
// Just execute - auto-connects on first use
execute_code({
  bot_name: "mybot",
  code: `
    const state = sdk.getState();
    console.log('Position:', state.player.worldX, state.player.worldZ);

    // Chop trees for 1 minute
    const endTime = Date.now() + 60_000;
    while (Date.now() < endTime) {
      const tree = sdk.findNearbyLoc(/^tree$/i);
      if (tree) await bot.chopTree(tree);
    }

    return sdk.getInventory();
  `,
});
```

See `mcp/README.md` for detailed API reference.

Code runs in an async context with `bot` (BotActions) and `sdk` (BotSDK) available as globals.

## Reporting SDK Bugs

When the SDK has a bug or rough edge, first find a workaround, then file a report. One command, no auth, no permission needed:

```bash
bun sdk/bug-report.ts "incorrect results from bot.foo(), had to use raw sdk.sendFoo() instead for xyz reason."
```

Important note: The game itself is extremely well tested and complete, it's not buggy. If you can't figure out how to do something, don't blame the game, blame your assumptions and keep investigating. File a bug report _after_ you figure out
what's going on, don't just assume the game is broken because you got confused, and give up. The SDK is a thin layer on top of the game, and the game is the source of truth.

After filing the bug, keep working on your goal!

## Session Workflow

This is a **persistent character** - you don't restart fresh each time. The workflow is:

### 1. Check World State First

Before writing any script, check where the bot is and what it has:

```bash
bun sdk/cli.ts {username}
```

This shows: position, inventory, skills, nearby NPCs/objects, and more.

**Exception**: Skip this if you just created the character and know it's at spawn.

**Tutorial Check**: If the character is in the tutorial area, call `await bot.skipTutorial()` before running any other scripts. The tutorial blocks normal gameplay.

### 2. Write Your Script

Edit `bots/{username}/script_name.ts` with your goal. Keep scripts focused on one task. you may write multiple scripts for different tasks and switch between them.

### 3. Run the Script

```bash
bun bots/{username}/script_name.ts
```

### 4. Observe and Iterate

Watch the output. After the script finishes (or fails), check state again:

```bash
bun sdk/cli.ts {username}
```

Record observations in `lab_log.md`, then improve the script.

### Chatting Without Taking Control

To talk in-game (or read chat) without disturbing whatever script currently
owns the bot, use the chat CLI — it connects in `observe` mode, which can send
chat (and nothing else) and never pre-empts (or gets pre-empted by) a
controller:

```bash
bun sdk/chat.ts {username} "meet me at the bank"   # send public chat
bun sdk/chat.ts {username} --to {player} "on my way"  # send a private message
bun sdk/chat.ts {username}                          # recent chat
bun sdk/chat.ts {username} --watch                  # tail live
```

Public chat is capped at 400 chars per message; `sdk.say()` auto-splits longer
text into wire-safe chunks.

Private messages (`sdk.dm(name, text)` / `sdk.sendPrivateMessage(name, msg)`)
reach the target anywhere in the world - no friends-list setup needed - and
show up in `getChat()` as type 3 (received) / 6 (sent). The server accepts one
social packet (say or PM) per tick; `dm()` paces its chunks automatically.

## Script Duration Guidelines

**Start short, extend as you gain confidence:**

| Duration      | Use When                                              |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| **10s**       | New script, single actions, untested logic, debugging |
| **30s-1 min** | Validated approach, building confidence               |
| **5+ min**    | Proven strategy, grinding runs. USE SPARINGLY         |

A failed 5-minute run wastes more time than five 30 second diagnostic runs. **Fail fast and start simple.**

Look out for "I can't reach" messages - the solution is often to open closed gates or that the item isn't accessible.

Read and grep in the learnings/ and wiki/ folder for tips, skill guides, item and npc locations, and shop information.

## SDK API Reference

For the complete method reference, see **[sdk/API.md](sdk/API.md)** (auto-generated from source).

**Quick overview:**

- `bot.*` - High-level actions that attempt to observe method-specific evidence (chopTree, walkTo, attack, etc.). Check a result when the method returns one.
- `sdk.*` - State queries and low-level browser-client dispatches. A successful `send*` result does not prove the game server applied the effect.

### bot.\* Quick Reference

| Method                          | What it does                                                     |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `walkTo(x, z, tolerance?)`      | Pathfind to coords, opens doors along the way                    |
| `talkTo(target)`                | Walk to NPC, start dialog                                        |
| `interactNpc(target, option?)`  | Walk to NPC, interact with any option (e.g. `'trade'`, `'fish'`) |
| `interactLoc(target, option?)`  | Walk to loc, interact with any option (e.g. `'mine'`, `'smelt'`) |
| `attack(target)`                | Walk to an NPC or player and start combat                    |
| `castSpell(target, spell)`      | Cast a combat spell on an NPC or player                         |
| `pickpocketNpc(target)`         | Pickpocket NPC, detects XP gain vs stun                          |
| `chopTree(target?)`             | Chop tree, wait for logs                                         |
| `pickupItem(target)`            | Pick up ground item                                              |
| `openDoor(target?)`             | Open a door or gate                                              |
| `openBank()`                    | Open nearest bank                                                |
| `depositItem(target, amount?)`  | Deposit item to bank                                             |

1: # SDK API Reference
2: 
3: > Auto-generated from TypeScript source. Do not edit directly.
4: > Run `bun run docs:api` to regenerate or `bun run docs:api:check` to verify it.
5: 
6: ## Execution model
7: 
8: - `bot.*` methods are high-level helpers. They attempt to observe method-specific evidence such as movement, inventory, XP, dialog, or state changes. When a method returns a result, inspect its `success` and any `reason` or `message`: the strength of completion evidence varies by method.
9: - `sdk.send*` methods are low-level browser-client dispatches. A successful `ActionResult` means the enhanced browser client accepted and dispatched the command; it does **not** prove that the game server processed it or that the intended game effect occurred.
10: - Methods whose signature returns `Promise<...>` are asynchronous and must be awaited. In particular, `scanNearbyLocs()` and `scanGroundItems()` return promises.
11: - `getInventory().length` is the number of occupied slots. `InventoryItem.count` is the quantity in that one slot, and `findInventoryItem()` returns the first matching slot rather than an aggregate across matching slots.
12: 
13: ## BotActions (high-level)
14: 
15: ### Grand Exchange
16: 
17: | Signature | Description |
18: |---|---|
19: | `async openGE(timeout: number = 15_000): Promise<GEActionResult>` | Walk to the physical exchange and open it. Requires updated client/server GE state support. |
20: | `async searchGE(query: string, side: 'buy' \| 'sell' = 'buy', timeout: number = 15_000): Promise<GEActionResult>` | Search the in-game catalogue in a free slot; returns acknowledged results in state.search. |
21: | `async placeGEOffer(request: GEOfferRequest, timeout: number = 30_000): Promise<GEActionResult>` | Place an inventory-funded offer at an already open exchange and verify the server receipt. Never retries confirmation. |
22: | `async cancelGEOffer(offerId: number, timeout: number = 15_000): Promise<GEActionResult>` | Cancel your offer's unfilled remainder; returned assets remain in collection. Uses offer ID, not slot. |
23: | `async collectGEOffer(offerId: number, notes: boolean = true, timeout: number = 15_000): Promise<GEActionResult>` | Collect one offer, optionally as notes. Reports actual backpack additions; overflow stays in collection. |
24: | `async collectGE(timeout: number = 15_000): Promise<GEActionResult>` | Collect every available claim as notes and coins; requires an open physical exchange. |
25: 
26: ### UI & Dialog
27: 
28: | Signature | Description |
29: |---|---|
30: | `async skipTutorial(options: { randomizeAppearance?: boolean } = {}): Promise<ActionResult>` | Skip tutorial by navigating dialogs and talking to tutorial NPCs. This is a porcelain method - domain logic that was moved from bot client. |
31: | `async dismissBlockingUI(): Promise<void>` | Dismiss any blocking UI like level-up dialogs. |
32: | `async waitForDialogClose(timeout: number = 30000): Promise<void>` | Wait for dialog to close. |
33: | `async navigateDialog(choices: (number \| string \| RegExp)[]): Promise<void>` | _No description provided._ |
34: 
35: ### Doors
36: 
37: | Signature | Description |
38: |---|---|
39: | `async openDoor(target?: NearbyLoc \| string \| RegExp): Promise<OpenDoorResult>` | Open a door or gate, walking to it if needed. |
40: 
41: ### Other
42: 
43: | Signature | Description |
44: |---|---|
45: | `async useItemOnLoc(item: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp, loc: NearbyLoc \| string \| RegExp, options: { timeout?: number } = {}): Promise<UseItemOnLocResult>` | Use an inventory item on a nearby location (e.g., fish on range, ore on furnace). Walks to the location first (handling doors), then uses the item. |
46: | `async useItemOnNpc(item: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp, npc: NearbyNpc \| string \| RegExp, options: { timeout?: number } = {}): Promise<UseItemOnNpcResult>` | Use an inventory item on a nearby NPC (e.g., bones on altar keeper, item on NPC). Walks to the NPC first (handling doors), then uses the item. |
47: | `async dropItem(target: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp, amount: number \| 'all' = 'all'): Promise<DropItemResult>` | Drop inventory items by name, waiting for each drop to land before sending the next. `sendDropItem` on a slot the server has already emptied silently no-ops, so slot loops built on stale state lose most of their sends; this re-resolves the slot from fresh state every time. `amount` counts inventory slots (a whole stack drops as one). Pass `'all'` or `-1` to drop every matching slot. |
48: | `async closeInterface(timeout: number = 5000): Promise<ActionResult>` | Close any open modal interface (bank, book, quest scroll, etc.). |
49: 
50: ### Woodcutting & Firemaking
51: 
52: | Signature | Description |
53: |---|---|
54: | `async chopTree(target?: NearbyLoc \| string \| RegExp): Promise<ChopTreeResult>` | Chop a tree and wait for logs to appear in inventory. |
55: | `async burnLogs(logsTarget?: InventoryItem \| string \| RegExp): Promise<BurnLogsResult>` | Burn logs using a tinderbox, wait for firemaking XP. |
56: 
57: ### Items & Inventory
58: 
59: | Signature | Description |
60: |---|---|
61: | `async pickupItem(target: GroundItem \| string \| RegExp): Promise<PickupResult>` | Pick up an item from the ground. |
62: 
63: ### NPC & Object Interaction
64: 
65: | Signature | Description |
66: |---|---|
67: | `async talkTo(target: NearbyNpc \| string \| RegExp): Promise<TalkResult>` | Talk to an NPC and wait for dialog to open. Walks to the NPC first (handling doors). |
68: | `async interactLoc(target: NearbyLoc \| string \| RegExp, option: number \| string \| RegExp = 1): Promise<InteractLocResult>` | Interact with a nearby location object (rock, fishing spot, furnace, etc.). Walks to the target first (handling doors), sends the interaction, then waits for an effect (animation, dialog, interface) or detects failure when the player has been idle for 2 ticks with nothing happening. Success can mean the action started, before its product arrives; use mineRock for completed mining. |
69: | `async interactNpc(target: NearbyNpc \| string \| RegExp, option: number \| string \| RegExp = 1): Promise<InteractNpcResult>` | Interact with a nearby NPC using a specified option (e.g. "Trade", "Pickpocket", "Fish"). Walks to the NPC first (handling doors), sends the interaction, then waits for an effect (animation, dialog, interface) or detects failure when the player has been idle for 2 ticks with nothing happening. |

### Player Trading

| Signature | Description |
|---|---|
| `async tradeWith(target: NearbyPlayer \| string \| RegExp, timeout: number = 30_000, options: { retryOnBusy?: boolean } = {}): Promise<ActionResult>` | Open a trade session with another player, walking closer if needed. Requesting a player who already requested you accepts their request; otherwise this waits (re-requesting periodically) until they request back or the timeout expires. The session is verified against the requested partner: a screen that opens with a *different* player (their pending request racing yours) is declined and the requested partner pursued until the deadline. `options.retryOnBusy` keeps retrying (with backoff) through "is busy at the moment" refusals instead of failing on the first one. |
| `async offerTradeItems(items: TradeItemSpec[], timeout: number = 15_000): Promise<ActionResult>` | Place items into your side of an open trade. Each spec resolves against your inventory; `amount` -1 offers all of that item (default 1). Waits until the offer window reflects each addition. Adding items resets both players' accepts server-side. |
| `async acceptTrade(timeout: number = 10_000): Promise<ActionResult>` | Accept the current trade screen and wait for observable progress: the screen advancing (offer -> confirm), the trade completing, or the acceptance being registered while waiting on the partner. A closed screen is classified: completed (`success: true`, `data.gave` / `data.received`) or declined (`success: false, reason: 'declined'`). |
| `async declineTrade(timeout: number = 5_000): Promise<ActionResult>` | Decline (close) the open trade and wait for the screen to close. Retries once if the first close landed during the offer->confirm transition (sendDeclineTrade refuses to send while no screen is open). |
| `async trade(target: NearbyPlayer \| string \| RegExp, options: TradeOptions = {}): Promise<TradeResult>` | Full trade happy path with one player: open the session, offer `give`, accept once the partner's offer satisfies `want` (or the `accept` predicate), re-verify on the confirm screen, and report the actual inventory delta. Any offer change resets both accepts server-side, so the offer seen at accept time is the offer that reaches the confirm screen; the confirm re-verification makes offer-switching structurally impossible to slip past this method. `options.requestTimeout` (default 30 s) bounds the trade request; `options.timeout` (default 60 s) bounds the open offer+confirm screens. Every close is classified as completed or declined, so `success: false` means nothing changed hands. |
| `async serveTrades(options: ServeTradesOptions = {}): Promise<ServeTradesResult>` | Serve incoming trades: wait for "wishes to trade with you." requests, accept ones matching the `from` filter, and run each session with the shared give/want/accept policy. The receiving half of a muling setup: ```ts // Worker: bot.trade('mule01', { give: [{ item: /ore/i, amount: -1 }] }) // Mule: bot.serveTrades({ from: /^fleet_/i, until: () => sdk.getInventory().length >= 26 }) ``` This owns the bot while running - it is an explicit serving loop, not a background hook, so it never fights another controller for the session. |

1: # Combat
2: 
3: Successful patterns for combat training.
4: 
5: ## Attacking NPCs
6: 
7: Use `bot.attack()` for cleaner code, or raw SDK for more control:
8: 
9: ```typescript
10: // Porcelain method (recommended)
11: const attack = await bot.attack(/cow/i);
12: if (!attack.success) console.warn(attack.reason, attack.message);
13: 
14: // Raw SDK dispatch (observe combat state afterwards)
15: const state = sdk.getState();
16: const npc = state?.nearbyNpcs.find(n => /cow/i.test(n.name));
17: const attackOpt = npc?.optionsWithIndex.find(o => /attack/i.test(o.text));
18: if (npc && attackOpt) {
19:     await sdk.sendInteractNpc(npc.index, attackOpt.opIndex);
20:     await sdk.waitForCondition(s => s.player?.combat.inCombat === true, 5_000);
21: }
22: ```
23: 
24: ## Combat Style Cycling
25: 
26: Combat-style indices depend on the equipped weapon the SDK reads
27: the table from the combat tab the server installed, so resolve indices from state
28: 
29: ```typescript
30: const targetSkill = 'Defence';
31: // A controlled style lists every skill it trains, so match against trainsSkills.
32: const style = sdk.getState()?.combatStyle?.styles.find(
33:     candidate => candidate.trainsSkills.includes(targetSkill),
34: );
35: if (!style) {
36:     throw new Error(`No ${targetSkill} style is available for the equipped weapon`);
37: }
38: await sdk.sendSetCombatStyle(style.index);
39: await sdk.waitForCondition(
40:     state => state.combatStyle?.currentStyle === style.index,
41:     5_000,
42: );
43: ```
44: 
45: ## Checking Combat State
46: 
47: ```typescript
48: const state = sdk.getState();
49: const inCombat = state?.player?.combat.inCombat ?? false;
50: 
51: // Animation is a useful heuristic, but is not specific to combat.
52: const isAnimating = (state?.player?.animId ?? -1) !== -1;
53: ```
54: 
55: ## Safe Training Locations
56: 
57: | Location | Coordinates | Targets | Notes |
58: |----------|-------------|---------|-------|
59: | Lumbridge cows | (3253, 3290) | Cows | Safe, good for all levels. South gate at (3253, 3266) |
60: | Lumbridge goblins | (3252, 3230) | Goblins, rats | Mixed enemies. Cluster runs NE from here — nothing at the old (3240, 3220) waypoint |
61: | Lumbridge chickens | (3237, 3295) | Chickens | Very safe, feathers drop |
62: | Al Kharid warriors | ~(3293, 3170) | `Al-Kharid warrior` (lvl 9) | Faster XP, kebabs nearby for food, can hit hard via multicombat vs low combat levels. |
63: 
64: ## Cow Field Details (Proven from 200+ kills)
65: 
66: The cow field is fenced with a gate on the south side:
67: - **Field center**: ~(3253, 3290)
68: - **South gate position**: (3253, 3266)
69: - **Inside cow pen**: x between 3242-3265, z between 3255-3298
70: 
71: ```typescript
72: function isInsideCowPen(x, z) {
73:     return x >= 3242 && x <= 3265 && z >= 3255 && z <= 3298;
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: ## Opening Gates
78: 
79: Cow field and chicken coop have fenced gates:
80: 
81: ```typescript
82: // Check for gate blocking path
83: const gate = sdk.getState()?.nearbyLocs.find(l => /gate/i.test(l.name));
84: if (gate) {
85:     const openOpt = gate.optionsWithIndex.find(o => /^open$/i.test(o.text));
86:     if (openOpt) {
87:         await bot.openDoor(gate);
88:     }
89: }
90: ```
91: 
92: ## Finding New Targets
93: 
94: After killing an NPC, find the next one quickly:
95: 
96: ```typescript
97: async function findTarget(pattern) {
98:     const state = sdk.getState();
99:     if (!state) return null;
100: 
101:     return state.nearbyNpcs
102:         .filter(n => pattern.test(n.name))
103:         .filter(n => n.optionsWithIndex.some(o => /attack/i.test(o.text)))
104:         .sort((a, b) => a.distance - b.distance)[0] ?? null;
105: }
106: ```
107: 
108: ## Looting Ground Items
109: 
110: **CRITICAL**: Use `sdk.scanGroundItems()` NOT `state.nearbyLocs` for dropped items!
111: 
112: ```typescript
113: // WRONG - nearbyLocs is for static objects (trees, rocks, etc.)
114: const wrongLoot = sdk.getState()?.nearbyLocs.filter(i => /hide/i.test(i.name));  // Won't work!
115: 
116: // CORRECT - scanGroundItems() for drops
117: const groundItems = await sdk.scanGroundItems();
118: const loot = groundItems.filter(i => /hide|bones|coins/i.test(i.name));
119: ```
120: 
121: ### Limit Pickups Per Loop
122: 
123: Pick up a few items (e.g. 3), then return to combat. Prevents getting stuck in infinite loot loops:
124: 
125: ```typescript
126: const MAX_PICKUPS = 3;
127: const groundItems = await sdk.scanGroundItems();
128: const loot = groundItems
129:     .filter(i => /hide|bones/i.test(i.name))
130:     .filter(i => i.distance < 5)
131:     .slice(0, MAX_PICKUPS);
132: 
133: for (const item of loot) {
134:     await bot.pickupItem(item);
135:     await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 500));
136: }
137: // Back to combat
138: ```
139: 
140: ## Error Handling for Long Runs (Critical!)
141: 
142: Timeouts and errors are frequent in crowded areas. Wrap attacks in try/catch:
143: 
144: ```typescript
145: // This pattern enabled consistent 10-minute runs
146: try {
147:     await bot.attack(/cow/i);
148: } catch (err) {
149:     console.log(`Attack timed out, trying next cow`);
150:     continue;  // Don't crash - just find another target
151: }
152: ```

154: ### Common Messages and Handling
155: 
156: | Message | Meaning | Response |
157: |---------|---------|----------|
158: | "I'm already under attack" | Crowded area, NPC in combat | Find different target |
159: | "I can't reach that!" | Obstacle or fence | Move closer, check gates |
160: | Attack timeout | Target died/moved | Try next NPC |
161: 
162: ### State Validation
163: 
164: Browser glitches sometimes return invalid positions. Validate state before acting:
165: 
166: ```typescript
167: const player = sdk.getState()?.player;
168: if (!player || player.worldX === 0 || player.worldZ === 0) {
169:     console.log('Invalid state - waiting for sync');
170:     await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 2000));
171:     continue;
172: }
173: 
174: // Also catch impossible position changes (>500 tiles = glitch)
175: if (Math.abs(player.worldX - lastX) > 500) {
176:     console.log('Position glitch detected, skipping action');
177:     continue;
178: }
179: ```
180: 
181: ## Auto-Train Lowest Combat Stat
182: 
183: For balanced progression, automatically train whichever stat is lowest:
184: 
185: ```typescript
186: function getLowestCombatStat(state) {
187:     const skills = state.skills;
188:     const atk = skills.find(s => s.name === 'Attack')?.baseLevel ?? 1;
189:     const str = skills.find(s => s.name === 'Strength')?.baseLevel ?? 1;
190:     const def = skills.find(s => s.name === 'Defence')?.baseLevel ?? 1;
191: 
192:     if (def <= atk && def <= str) return 'Defence';
193:     if (str <= atk) return 'Strength';
194:     return 'Attack';
195: }
196: 
197: const state = sdk.getState();
198: if (!state) throw new Error('No world state');
199: const stat = getLowestCombatStat(state);
200: const style = state.combatStyle?.styles.find(option => option.trainsSkills.includes(stat));
201: if (!style) throw new Error(`No style trains ${stat} with the equipped weapon`);
202: await sdk.sendSetCombatStyle(style.index);
203: console.log(`Training ${stat} with ${style.name}`);
204: ```
205: 
206: This pattern enabled balanced 60+ in all melee stats.

1: # Dialogs & UI
2: 
3: Successful patterns for handling game dialogs and interfaces.
4: 
5: ## Dismissing Level-Up Dialogs
6: 
7: Level-up dialogs block all actions. Dismiss them immediately:
8: 
9: ```typescript
10: if (sdk.getState()?.dialog.isOpen) {
11:   await sdk.sendClickDialog(0);
12:   continue; // Skip rest of loop iteration
13: }
14: ```
15: 
16: ## Dismiss at Arc Start
17: 
18: All BotActions methods automatically dismiss blocking UI before executing. Manual dismissal is only needed when using low-level sdk methods directly:
19: 
20: ```typescript
21: await bot.dismissBlockingUI();
22: ```
23: 
24: ## Checking Dialog State
25: 
26: ```typescript
27: const dialog = sdk.getState()?.dialog;
28: 
29: // Is any dialog open?
30: if (dialog.isOpen) { ... }
31: 
32: // Is dialog waiting for input?
33: if (dialog.isOpen && !dialog.isWaiting) { ... }
34: 
35: // Get available options
36: for (const opt of dialog.options) {
37:     console.log(`${opt.index}: ${opt.text}`);
38: }
39: ```
40: 
41: ## Navigating Multi-Step Dialogs
42: 
43: For NPC conversations with choices:
44: 
45: ```typescript
46: // Click through until specific option appears
47: for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
48:   const s = sdk.getState();
49:   if (!s?.dialog.isOpen) {
50:     await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 150));
51:     continue;
52:   }
53: 
54:   // Look for target option
55:   const targetOpt = s.dialog.options.find((o) => /yes/i.test(o.text));
56:   if (targetOpt) {
57:     await sdk.sendClickDialog(targetOpt.index);
58:     break;
59:   }
60: 
61:   // Otherwise click to continue
62:   await sdk.sendClickDialog(0);
63:   await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 200));
64: }
65: ```
66: 
67: ## Shop Interfaces
68: 
69: ```typescript
70: const state = sdk.getState();
71: if (!state) throw new Error('No world state');
72: 
73: // Check if shop is open
74: if (state.shop.isOpen) { ... }
75: 
76: // Check if any interface is open (bank, shop, etc.)
77: if (state.interface?.isOpen) { ... }
78: ```
79: 
80: ## sendClickDialog Index Behavior
81: 
82: - `sendClickDialog(0)` = special "continue" action (RESUME_PAUSEBUTTON)
83: - `sendClickDialog(1-5)` = click actual option buttons (1-based indices)
84: 
85: Always use `0` as fallback for "Click here to continue" screens.
86: 
87: ## Al Kharid Toll Gate Pattern
88: 
89: Requires 10gp. Position west of gate: (3267, 3228).
90: 
91: ```typescript
92: const gate = sdk.getState()?.nearbyLocs.find((l) => /gate/i.test(l.name));
93: if (!gate) throw new Error('No gate nearby');
94: await sdk.sendInteractLoc(gate.x, gate.z, gate.id, 1);
95: await sdk.waitForTicks(2);
96: 
97: // Click through dialog: 0 = continue, or pick "Yes" when available
98: for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
99:   const yesOpt = sdk
100:     .getState()
101:     ?.dialog?.options.find((o) => /yes/i.test(o.text));
102:   await sdk.sendClickDialog(yesOpt?.index ?? 0);
103:   await sdk.waitForTicks(1);
104: }
105: 
106: await bot.walkTo(3277, 3227); // Walk through to Al Kharid
107: ```
108: 
109: ## Buying Kebabs from the Kebab Seller (Al Kharid)
110: 
111: Sells kebabs via dialog (not a shop interface). Location: (3273, 3180), spawns at (3272, 3182).
112: 
113: ```typescript
114: // Walk to kebab seller
115: await bot.walkTo(3273, 3180);
116: 
117: // Find the kebab seller
118: const seller = sdk
119:   .getState()
120:   ?.nearbyNpcs.find((n) => /kebab/i.test(n.name));
121: if (!seller) throw new Error('No kebab seller nearby');
122: const talkOpt = seller.optionsWithIndex.find((o) => /talk/i.test(o.text));
123: if (!talkOpt) throw new Error('Kebab seller has no Talk-to option');
124: await sdk.sendInteractNpc(seller.index, talkOpt.opIndex);
125: await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1000));
126: 
127: // Handle dialog to buy kebab (1gp each)
128: for (let i = 0; i < 15; i++) {
129:   const s = sdk.getState();
130:   if (!s?.dialog.isOpen) {
131:     await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 200));
132:     continue;
133:   }
134:   const buyOpt = s.dialog.options.find((o) => /yes/i.test(o.text));
135:   if (buyOpt) {
136:     await sdk.sendClickDialog(buyOpt.index);
137:     break;
138:   }
139:   await sdk.sendClickDialog(0);
140:   await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 300));
141: }
142: ```
143: 
144: Kebabs cost 1gp and heal 1-19 HP (random). Good cheap food for training.
145: 
146: ## Detecting Stuck in Dialog
147: 
148: If your script makes no progress, check for stuck dialogs:
149: 
150: ```typescript
151: // In your main loop
152: if (sdk.getState()?.dialog.isOpen) {
153:   console.log("Dialog open, dismissing...");
154:   await sdk.sendClickDialog(0);
155:   continue;
156: }
157: ```

1: # Walking & Navigation
2: 
3: Successful patterns for movement and pathfinding.
4: 
5: ## Basic Walking
6: 
7: `bot.walkTo()` performs pathfinding for both short and long routes:
8: 
9: ```typescript
10: const result = await bot.walkTo(3222, 3218);  // Walk to Lumbridge
11: if (!result.success) console.warn(result.reason, result.message);
12: ```
13: 
14: ## Long Distance Walking
15: 
16: `walkTo()` supports long routes. Use waypoints when you intentionally need a
17: safer route, want progress checkpoints, or need to avoid a dangerous area:
18: 
19: ```typescript
20: const WAYPOINTS_TO_BANK = [
21:     { x: 3270, z: 3380 },  // Step 1
22:     { x: 3250, z: 3395 },  // Step 2
23:     { x: 3230, z: 3410 },  // Step 3
24:     { x: 3210, z: 3425 },  // Step 4
25:     { x: 3185, z: 3436 },  // Final destination
26: ];
27: 
28: async function walkWaypoints(waypoints) {
29:     for (const wp of waypoints) {
30:         // Try up to 3 times per waypoint
31:         for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {
32:             await bot.walkTo(wp.x, wp.z);
33:             await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 500));
34: 
35:             const player = sdk.getState()?.player;
36:             const dist = Math.sqrt(
37:                 Math.pow(player.worldX - wp.x, 2) +
38:                 Math.pow(player.worldZ - wp.z, 2)
39:             );
40: 
41:             if (dist <= 5) break;  // Close enough
42:         }
43:     }
44: }
45: ```
46: 
47: ## Verifying Arrival
48: 
49: Always check if you actually arrived:
50: 
51: ```typescript
52: const result = await bot.walkTo(targetX, targetZ);
53: 
54: const player = sdk.getState()?.player;
55: const dist = Math.sqrt(
56:     Math.pow(player.worldX - targetX, 2) +
57:     Math.pow(player.worldZ - targetZ, 2)
58: );
59: 
60: if (dist > 5) {
61:     console.warn(`Walk failed: still ${dist.toFixed(0)} tiles away`);
62: }
63: ```
64: 
65: ## Known Routes
66: 
67: ### Varrock Mine to Varrock West Bank (~100 tiles)
68: 
69: ```typescript
70: const MINE_TO_BANK = [
71:     { x: 3270, z: 3380 },
72:     { x: 3250, z: 3395 },
73:     { x: 3230, z: 3410 },
74:     { x: 3210, z: 3425 },
75:     { x: 3185, z: 3436 },
76: ];
77: 
78: const BANK_TO_MINE = [
79:     { x: 3210, z: 3425 },
80:     { x: 3230, z: 3410 },
81:     { x: 3250, z: 3395 },
82:     { x: 3270, z: 3380 },
83:     { x: 3285, z: 3365 },
84: ];
85: ```
86: 
87: ## Opening Obstacles
88: 
89: `bot.walkTo()` attempts to open doors and gates on its route. If a route fails,
90: inspect nearby objects and open the specific obstacle before retrying:
91: 
92: ```typescript
93: let result = await bot.walkTo(3250, 3260);
94: if (!result.success) {
95:     const gate = sdk.findNearbyLoc(/^gate$/i);
96:     if (gate?.optionsWithIndex.some(option => /^open$/i.test(option.text))) {
97:         await bot.openDoor(gate);
98:         result = await bot.walkTo(3250, 3260);
99:     }
100: }
101: ```

103:

109: Draynor Bank (3092, 3243) is the closest bank to Lumbridge cow field.

112: **AVOID** the area around (3220, 3220) - aggressive Dark Wizards here will attack and likely kill characters under combat level 20.

115: Stay **north of z=3240** when walking west from cow field to Draynor. Use `walkTo` with intermediate points that curve north around the danger zone rather than walking in a straight line.

1: # Fishing
2: 
3: Successful patterns for fishing automation.
4: 
5: ## Finding Fishing Spots
6: 
7: Fishing spots are **NPCs**, not locations:
8: 
9: ```typescript
10: const spot = sdk.getState()?.nearbyNpcs.find((npc) => /fishing\s*spot/i.test(npc.name));
11: ```
12: 
13: ## Spot Types Matter
14: 
15: Different spots have different level requirements:
16: 
17: | Spot Options | Fish Type           | Level |
18: | ------------ | ------------------- | ----- |
19: | Net, Bait    | Shrimp, anchovies   | 1+    |
20: | Net, Harpoon | Mackerel, cod, bass | 16+   |
21: | Lure, Bait   | Trout, salmon       | 20+   |
22: 
23: Filter for the right spot type:
24: 
25: ```typescript
26: // Level 1 fishing - need "Bait" option (indicates small net spot)
27: const fishingSpots = sdk.getState()?.nearbyNpcs.filter(
28:   npc => /fishing\s*spot/i.test(npc.name),
29: ) ?? [];
30: const smallNetSpots = fishingSpots.filter((npc) =>
31:   npc.optionsWithIndex.some((opt) => /^bait$/i.test(opt.text)),
32: );
33: ```
34: 
35: ## Fishing Action
36: 
37: ```typescript
38: const spot = sdk.getState()?.nearbyNpcs.find((npc) => /fishing\s*spot/i.test(npc.name));
39: const netOpt = spot?.optionsWithIndex.find((o) => /^net$/i.test(o.text));
40: if (spot && netOpt) await sdk.sendInteractNpc(spot.index, netOpt.opIndex);
41: ```
42: 
43: ## Continuous Clicking Works
44: 
45: Don't over-engineer wait conditions. Just keep clicking:
46: 
47: ```typescript
48: while (true) {
49:   const state = sdk.getState();
50:   if (!state) {
51:     await sdk.waitForStateUpdate();
52:     continue;
53:   }
54: 
55:   // Dismiss any dialogs (level-ups)
56:   if (state.dialog.isOpen) {
57:     await sdk.sendClickDialog(0);
58:     continue;
59:   }
60: 
61:   const spot = state.nearbyNpcs.find((npc) => /fishing\s*spot/i.test(npc.name));
62:   if (spot) {
63:     const netOpt = spot.optionsWithIndex.find((o) => /^net$/i.test(o.text));
64:     if (netOpt) await sdk.sendInteractNpc(spot.index, netOpt.opIndex);
65:   }
66: 
67:   await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1000));
68: }
69: ```
70: 
71: ## Safe Fishing Locations
72: 
73: | Location            | Coordinates      | Spot Type    | Notes                                                                                                                                     |
74: | ------------------- | ---------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
75: | **Draynor Village** | **(3087, 3230)** | **Net/Bait** | **USE THIS for level 1.** Shrimp/anchovies. Dark wizards at (3084, 3236)/(3085, 3238) — stay south of z≈3232 if you are low combat level! |
76: | Al Kharid river     | (3267, 3148)     | Lure/Bait    | Fly fishing (level 20+). 10gp toll gate to reach. Watch for a lvl 14 scorpion.                                                            |
77: | Barbarian Village   | (3110, 3434)     | Lure/Bait    | Fly fishing (level 20+). Second spot at (3104, 3424).                                                                                     |
78: 
79: **COMMON MISTAKE**: Lumbridge area (3238, 3251) has NO level-1 fishing spots. Use Draynor!
80: 
81: **COMMON MISTAKE**: Lumbridge Swamp **(3239, 3147)** has NO fishing spots _at all_ — not net, not lure/bait. Verified against map spawn data: nearest spot is 28 tiles east at (3267, 3148) across the toll gate. Do not walk here to fish.
82: 
83: ## Handling Drift
84: 
85: Fishing spots move. Check distance and walk back if needed:
86: 
87: ```typescript
88: const START_AREA = { x: 3087, z: 3230 };
89: const MAX_DRIFT = 15;
90: 
91: const player = sdk.getState()?.player;
92: if (!player) throw new Error('No player state');
93: const drift = Math.sqrt(
94:   Math.pow(player.worldX - START_AREA.x, 2) +
95:     Math.pow(player.worldZ - START_AREA.z, 2),
96: );
97: 
98: if (drift > MAX_DRIFT) {
99:   console.log(`Drifted ${drift.toFixed(0)} tiles, walking back`);
100:   await bot.walkTo(START_AREA.x, START_AREA.z);
101: }
102: ```

display.text:
# Cooking

## Cooking on a Range

Use `bot.useItemOnLoc(item, loc)` with raw food on a range:

```typescript
const raw = sdk.findInventoryItem(/^raw shrimps$/i);
const range = sdk.findNearbyLoc(/^range$/i);
if (raw && range) {
  await bot.useItemOnLoc(raw, range);
}
```

## Range Locations

| Location | Coordinates | Loc name | Notes |
|----------|-------------|----------|-------|
| **Lumbridge (near Bob's Axes)** | **(3230, 3196)** | `Range` | **USE THIS.** No quest needed. Just south of Bob's Axes (3232, 3203). |
| Lumbridge Castle kitchen | (3212, 3215) | `Cooking range` | **REQUIRES Cook's Assistant quest completion.** The Cook stands next to it at (3209, 3215). |
| Al Kharid (Karim's kebab shop) | (3271, 3180) | `Range` | No quest needed, but 10gp toll gate to get there. |

**COMMON MISTAKE**: The range inside Lumbridge Castle kitchen — **(3212, 3215)**, ground floor, SW corner where the Cook stands — is locked behind the Cook's Assistant quest. Without the quest the Cook says *"Hey! Who said you could use that?"* and nothing cooks. Use the Range at (3230, 3196), south of Bob's Brilliant Axes, instead.

**Name gotcha**: the quest-gated castle range is named `Cooking range`, not `Range`, so `/^range$/i` deliberately skips it. Usable cooking sources are `Range` (loc 2728-2731), `Fireplace` (2724-2726), `Cooking pot` (2727), and `Fire` (2732) — a wider match is:

```typescript
const source = sdk.findNearbyLoc(/^(range|fireplace|fire|cooking pot)$/i);
```

Nearest usable sources elsewhere: Fireplace (3205, 3220) in Lumbridge castle, Cooking pot (3232, 3238), Fire (3245, 3246), Fireplace (3100, 3256) near Draynor.
